references.text: Moses gathered the whole congregation of Israel and spoke to them, showing the same pattern where the people assemble before Moses to receive instructions.
The beginning of the same chapter where Moses gathers the whole congregation of Israel, which is the context for their now going out from his presence.
Moses speaks to the whole congregation of Israel about the gifts for the tabernacle, which is the message the people respond to by going out.
The people bring voluntary offerings after they have gone out from Moses, showing the result of the gathering described in 35:20.
Korah gathered the whole congregation against Moses, a parallel use of the expression 'the whole congregation of the children of Israel'.
Both verses illustrate the theological principle that 'as the Lord had spoken to Moses, so did the children of Israel'.
A profound parallel showing that the whole congregation always acts according to the Lord's command, whether it concerns grace or judgment.
Highlights the theological theme of the collective movement and unity of 'the whole congregation' under God's leadership in the wilderness.
